title: Partner Terms & Confidentiality
summary: Partner master agreement for onboarding; applicable service schedules also apply.
body:
CA APPROVED FOR PUBLICATION OR SIGNATURE
Source: Version 2.2, 18 November 2026 | Sections 1–6, 9

1. Parties, scope and document precedence

This Agreement is proposed between Mumma’s Nest Private Limited, CIN U47820PN2024PTC232854, at Blue Ridge T-7, Flat 702, Hinjawadi, Pune, Maharashtra 411057, India, operating the “SuiSakhi” platform (subject to verification of entity, address, GST and contracting authority), and the individual or legal entity identified in the Partner Registration Form (“Partner”).

The Agreement applies only to the categories selected and approved during onboarding: (A) Stitching/Alterations, (B) Garment Care, (C) Measurement, (D) Wardrobe/Quick Care & Doorstep Services, (E) Bulk/Wedding Orders, (F) Pickup & Delivery, (G) Fashion Brands/Accessories, and (H) Dress Rental. An applicable Category Schedule and Commercial Schedule must be accepted before assignments or listings go live.

Order of precedence for conflicts: (1) mandatory law and non-waivable consumer rights; (2) signed negotiated addendum for the relevant category; (3) the applicable Category and Commercial Schedules; (4) this Master Agreement; (5) accepted order-specific instructions; (6) Annexure 0 historical CA CA Approved (reference only, not operative once Version 2.0 is executed). No unilateral task instruction can override pricing, statutory rights or agreed risk allocation.

2. Partner onboarding and engagement

2.1 Verification. Partner shall provide accurate legal name, business constitution, address, authorized representative, bank details, PAN/GST and other legally required registrations, licenses and verification materials. SuiSakhi may validate and suspend activation for material deficiencies. Verification does not guarantee safety or performance.

2.2 Independent status. Unless separately agreed in writing and consistent with actual working arrangements, Partner operates as an independent service provider or seller and is responsible for its staff, payroll, permissions, equipment and statutory obligations. No agency to bind SuiSakhi is created.

2.3 Personnel. Only approved and appropriately trained personnel may access customers, property or order information. Subcontracting and substitutions require prior approval and equivalent confidentiality, safety and insurance commitments.

2.4 Conduct. No harassment, theft, intimidation, intoxication while serving customers, unauthorized entry, recording or use of customer data. Partner must follow reasonable safety, hygiene, service and anti-fraud standards and promptly report incidents.

2.5 No off-platform diversion. Partner shall not divert an active SuiSakhi order or misuse SuiSakhi confidential leads, customer data or order details to bypass agreed fees. Any post-termination restriction must be narrowly CA Approveded and vetted for enforceability under Indian law.

3. Payment model and settlement

3.1 Model A — Core services. For stitching, alterations, garment care, measurements, doorstep/wardrobe services, bulk orders and delivery, the customer pays via SuiSakhi checkout. SuiSakhi administers order confirmation, completion review, refunds and partner payout instructions through a compliant authorized payment provider. The payment provider, not an unregulated SuiSakhi account, shall hold or settle funds as legally permitted.

3.2 Normal release. For ordinary completed Model A orders, SuiSakhi proposes instructing partner payout within 24–48 hours after customer-confirmed completion or expiry of a disclosed objective acceptance window, subject to banking days, payment-provider rules, legally required settlement timelines and the Commercial Schedule. Lack of customer response alone shall not permit indefinite withholding.

3.3 Disputes. Upon a documented credible complaint, SuiSakhi may request a temporary hold only over a reasonable disputed amount where contractually and legally permitted. Partner receives notice, evidence summary and opportunity to respond; undisputed amounts are paid on schedule. Define review target 30 Days, appeal route and outer release deadline in the Commercial Schedule. No allegation alone proves wrongdoing.

3.4 Model B — Brand/accessory/rental marketplace. For fashion brands, accessories and dress rentals, the customer pays once through an approved marketplace checkout and an authorized provider splits or settles the net merchandise/rental proceeds to the selling Partner and agreed platform fees to SuiSakhi, if supported. Brand sets approved catalogue prices, owns inventory, packs and fulfils orders, and is the disclosed seller; SuiSakhi’s exact role, invoicing, returns and consumer obligations are set out in the category schedule.

3.5 Commercial terms. For each category, a signed schedule must state commission or fixed fee, tax treatment, invoice issuer, gateway costs, refund and chargeback allocations, deductions, payout account, timelines, settlement reports, cancellations and effective date. No retrospective fee change on accepted orders.

3.6 No promise of escrow. Neither party shall describe the arrangement as escrow, guaranteed protection or an unrestricted right to hold money unless expressly authorized by the payment provider and law. Payment architecture and any reserves require gateway and legal sign-off.

3.7 Refunds and recovery. SuiSakhi may coordinate legally required refunds and approved rework. Any partner recovery, offset or reserve must be evidence-based, proportionate and permitted by the commercial schedule; partners may dispute adjustments. Customer statutory rights are unaffected.

4. Customer property, quality and liability

4.1 Care and documentation. Partner shall inspect reasonably apparent condition, record item count, descriptions, customer-approved measurements and material risk notices; obtain consent for narrowly scoped photographs; maintain pickup, custody and handover proof.

4.2 Fabric and garment risks. Partner shall check care labels and apparent dye instability, shrinkage, embellishments, fragile seams and fabric limitations. Obtain informed consent for material risks or decline unsafe treatment. Consent to inherent risk never excuses negligent processing, incorrect cutting or failure to follow agreed specifications.

4.3 Home visits. Partner accesses only authorized areas, verifies identity, records check-in/out, and never handles unrelated valuables. Customers should secure valuables and identify work areas. SuiSakhi will investigate missing-property allegations fairly; a disclaimer does not exclude proven theft, negligence or non-waivable liability.

4.4 Remedies. Documented service deficiency may lead to correction, re-performance, replacement, refund or other lawful remedy based on causation, evidence and feasibility. No automatic fixed liability cap for serious misconduct; negotiated limits, if any, require counsel approval.

4.5 Insurance. Partner shall maintain insurance stated in its category schedule where applicable (e.g. goods in custody/transit, public liability, professional/product liability). Coverage, deductibles and exclusions shall be recorded and verified; insurance does not replace contractual responsibility.

4.6 Claims process. Incident reporting within 24 Hrs after discovery; preserve records and cooperate. SuiSakhi shall hear both sides, record reasoned findings and provide escalation. A customer complaint alone is not proof of partner liability.

5. Privacy, intellectual property and platform controls

5.1 Personal information. Use customer names, addresses, measurements, photos and order data only as authorized for assigned orders. Apply device security, least-privilege access, approved communication channels, secure deletion and prompt breach notification within 24 Hrs. The exact controller/fiduciary and processor roles and effective Indian privacy-law requirements must be confirmed by counsel for each model.

5.2 Designs and content. Customer designs and measurements remain subject to their lawful rights. Partner may not reuse or publicize customer designs or images without permission. Brand grants SuiSakhi a limited, revocable license during listing to display approved trademarks, descriptions and images; Partner warrants rights to submitted materials.

5.3 Communication. Use approved in-app or masked channels when available. Do not harvest contacts or market directly using order information. Emergency and lawful customer communications remain permitted.

5.4 Records. Maintain proportionate audit trails, consents, payment allocations, shipment/visit evidence and complaints for the lawful retention period [TO CONFIRM].

6. Performance, term, suspension and dispute resolution

6.1 Performance. Follow agreed specifications, timelines, hygiene and customer service standards. Material deviations, substitutions or price increases require documented customer approval.

6.2 Suspension. SuiSakhi may pause assignments/listings for credible safety, fraud, privacy or repeated service-quality concerns while investigating. Provide notice and an opportunity to respond unless immediate protective action is needed.

6.3 Exit. Either party may terminate with [NOTICE PERIOD] written notice; immediate termination for serious misconduct or material breach as legally permitted. Complete or reassign pending orders, return property, withdraw access, securely handle data and settle undisputed sums.

6.4 Indemnity. Each party is responsible for its own fraud, wilful misconduct, negligence and legal non-compliance, subject to negotiated indemnities and liability limits approved by counsel. Nothing removes non-waivable consumer or statutory rights.

6.5 Governing law. Indian law applies. Subject to mandatory statutory forums, parties propose competent courts in Pune, Maharashtra. Partner support and grievance details: [CONFIRM].

9. Electronic acceptance and evidence

Partner selects category and legal entity, verifies authority, reviews Master Agreement plus all applicable Category and Commercial Schedules, and affirmatively accepts each required document. Record name, mobile/verified login, legal entity, signatory capacity, agreement/schedule version or hash, timestamp, consent text and audit metadata. New material terms require fresh acceptance for future orders. Electronic execution and stamping requirements to be confirmed by counsel.

title: Home Visit & Personal Safety — Partner Addendum
summary: Safety requirements for eligible home visits, measurements and doorstep work.
body:
CA APPROVED FOR PUBLICATION OR SIGNATURE
Source: Version 2.2, 18 November 2026 | Section 6A.1–6A.9

6A. Home Visit, Measurement & Personal Safety Protocol — proposed mandatory addendum

Applicability. This protocol applies to measurement partners, wardrobe/home-service partners, pickup/delivery personnel entering residential premises, their staff and any approved substitutes. It supplements, and does not replace, the Master Agreement, applicable law and customer rights.

6A.1 Eligibility and vetting. Before residential assignments, SuiSakhi may require proportionate identity/address verification, reference checks, role-specific training, and lawful background verification. Partners shall not assign unapproved personnel or substitute a different individual without platform approval and customer notification.

6A.2 Customer choice and visit eligibility. Customers must see the assigned professional’s verified name, photograph, role and applicable safety requirements before the visit. A customer may refuse entry or request reassignment for a safety concern without penalty. No partner may pressure the customer to admit them. For designated higher-risk appointments, an adult chaperone must be present; if absent, the visit shall not start and shall be safely rescheduled. SuiSakhi must clearly communicate such requirements before booking.

6A.3 Body measurement safeguard. For measurements involving the body, SuiSakhi shall offer a female measurement professional as the default where available, and must not confirm a booking that cannot meet the customer’s selected safety conditions. An adult customer may affirmatively choose a male measurement professional, but the visit shall proceed only with another adult present as chaperone. Partner must explain each measurement, obtain specific voluntary consent before any contact, offer self-measurement or over-clothing methods where feasible, and stop immediately on request. No intimate-area touching, undressing requests, unnecessary photography, or private-room isolation. Measurements of minors require parent/guardian presence and an appropriately approved professional; no one-to-one visits.

6A.4 Wardrobe and doorstep services. Work is limited to the agreed rooms, cupboards and tasks. No handling of cash, jewellery, documents or unrelated belongings. For visits designated higher-risk by the service protocol, another adult must be present regardless of the partner’s gender. If safety conditions are not met, partner must leave safely, log the reason without collecting intrusive personal details, and request rescheduling.

6A.5 Conduct and privacy. No sexual comments, harassment, discriminatory remarks, personal propositions, requests for private contact, off-platform meetings, unauthorized recording or photography, or disclosure of customer location, measurements or household circumstances. Do not ask whether the customer lives alone or request personal information unrelated to the order. No personal phone photography; use only approved in-app capture with consent and purpose limitation.

6A.6 Visit controls. Verify identity at arrival; use platform check-in/check-out and customer-approved service scope; no unannounced personnel; no locked-door or isolated measurement sessions; no after-hours visits outside approved windows. Provide an accessible in-app safety contact and emergency escalation. GPS, where used, must be proportionate, disclosed and subject to retention limits.

6A.7 Incidents and complaints. Immediately stop the service and prioritize personal safety. The partner must report threats, harassment, inappropriate contact, property incidents or other serious concerns through the emergency/escalation channel promptly; where a crime or imminent danger is suspected, contact appropriate emergency services. SuiSakhi may temporarily suspend new assignments while preserving evidence, supporting the complainant, hearing relevant parties fairly and cooperating with lawful authorities. No retaliation, evidence tampering or private settlement pressure.

6A.8 Liability and remedies. Partners remain responsible for their own proven misconduct and that of authorized personnel, subject to applicable law. SuiSakhi shall apply reasonable onboarding, supervision, response and grievance controls and shall not disclaim liability for its own negligence or other non-excludable obligations. Customer safety acknowledgements do not waive statutory rights, nor does an allegation alone establish guilt.

6A.9 Training, acceptance and enforcement. Before receiving eligible assignments, each individual partner must accept this addendum electronically, complete safety training and pass required checks. The platform shall record agreement version, identity, time and category. Material breaches may lead to immediate suspension, investigation, termination and referral to authorities where appropriate.

title: Partner Verification & Criminal Record Declaration
body:
CA APPROVED FOR PUBLICATION OR SIGNATURE
Source: Version 2.2, 18 November 2026 | Annexure 1 additional clauses, pages 12–13

Verification and Consent. Before onboarding, and from time to time afterwards, SuiSakhi, or a verification agency it appoints, may verify your identity, address and criminal record, including through police verification or a police clearance certificate. You consent to this and will give the documents and information needed, promptly and accurately. SuiSakhi uses this information only to verify you, to keep customers safe and to meet legal duties, and handles it under its Privacy Notice and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.

Undertaking. You declare and undertake that:

you have not been convicted of, and have no pending criminal case, charge sheet or trial for, any offence involving theft, cheating, criminal breach of trust, fraud, violence, harassment, any offence against a woman or child, any sexual offence, or any other offence involving dishonesty, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (and, for older offences, the Indian Penal Code, 1860) or any other law in force, except what you have disclosed to SuiSakhi in writing before accepting this agreement and SuiSakhi has accepted in writing;

all information and documents you give for verification are true, complete and not misleading; and

the same is true of every employee, helper or other person you assign to an Order, and you will not assign anyone who has not been verified.

Immediate termination. SuiSakhi may suspend you, and may terminate this agreement with immediate effect and without notice or warning, if verification is not completed or is adverse, if your declaration or any information or document you gave is false or incomplete, if you fail to give the notice above, or if you are charged with or convicted of an offence of the kind listed above. An arrest or complaint alone does not mean you are guilty. SuiSakhi will consider the facts and may suspend you while the matter is decided.

Legal action. Giving false information or documents, or committing an offence while providing services, may be reported to the police and dealt with under applicable law, including the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and, where relevant, the Information Technology Act, 2000. SuiSakhi may also claim compensation. These steps are in addition to its other rights under this agreement.

title: Home Visit & Personal Safety Policy
summary: Customer-facing overview for home visits and personal safety.
body:
CA APPROVED FOR PUBLICATION OR SIGNATURE
Source: Version 2.2, 18 November 2026 | Sections 4.3, 6A.2, 6A.4, 6A.7–8

Before a home visit, check the assigned professional’s identity and the applicable safety requirements. You may refuse entry or request reassignment for a safety concern without penalty. Keep valuables secure and identify the agreed work areas. For designated higher-risk visits another adult must be present; otherwise reschedule. Partners must not handle unrelated valuables. Report safety or missing-property concerns to SuiSakhi; in an emergency contact emergency services. Complaints will be investigated fairly. Your statutory rights are not waived.

title: Measurement Safety & Consent
summary: Customer-facing overview for measurement safety and consent.
body:
CA APPROVED FOR PUBLICATION OR SIGNATURE
Source: Version 2.2, 18 November 2026 | Section 6A.2–3, 6A.10

A female measurement professional is the default where available. An adult customer may affirmatively choose a male professional only with another adult present as chaperone. The professional must explain each measurement, obtain specific voluntary consent before contact and stop on request. No intimate-area touching, undressing requests or unnecessary photography. For minors, a parent or guardian must be present and the professional appropriately approved. You may refuse entry or stop the service. Your legal rights remain unaffected.

title: Fabric, Garment Damage & Loss Policy
summary: Customer-facing overview for fabric, garment damage and loss.
body:
CA APPROVED FOR PUBLICATION OR SIGNATURE
Source: Version 2.2, 18 November 2026 | Sections 4.1–4.6, 7A–B

Partners must inspect reasonably apparent fabric or garment condition and disclose material risks, including dye instability, shrinkage and fragile seams. Informed approval is required for materially risky treatment, or the partner may decline it. Acceptance of inherent risk does not excuse negligent handling or incorrect cutting. Report damage or loss to SuiSakhi for evidence-based review. Depending on the findings, lawful remedies may include correction, re-performance, replacement or refund.

CA APPROVED FOR PUBLICATION OR SIGNATURE
